proposed_comments.title: Carry a failure flag through deferred icon requests

confidence.rationale: The current request completion path only sees Value = null after provider exceptions, so it cannot distinguish failures from genuine empty results without an explicit flag.

proposed_comments.title: Mark provider exceptions as failed requests

confidence.rationale: The provider catch path is the only place in this flow that converts an exception into a null result before the deferred request completes.

proposed_comments.body:
### Mark provider exceptions as failed requests

**Severity:** `medium`

The `IconProvider.SourceRequestedCore` catch block currently logs and clears `Value`, but it never marks the request as failed. Once the failure flag exists, please set it here as well so the caller can clear the icon and record `Failed` instead of treating loader exceptions as empty results.

proposed_comments.title: Reject stale same-key refreshes and failed provider results

confidence.rationale: The current stale guard checks only SourceKey identity even though requestVersion changes on each refresh, so same-key refreshes can still apply older results.

proposed_comments.title: Attach the winning cached request before other callers observe the in-flight load

confidence.rationale: The current code publishes the shared in-flight task before the winning request has fully attached its diagnostics state, which can leave concurrent in-flight resolutions without a linked load.

proposed_comments.body:
### Attach the winning cached request before other callers observe the in-flight load

**Severity:** `medium`

`CachedIconSourceProvider.GetOrCreateSlowPath` publishes the shared in-flight task before the winning requester has finished attaching its diagnostics state. A concurrent caller can therefore record an `InFlight` resolution without a linked load, and a fast worker can skew the new demand metrics before the winning request is fully attributed. Please make the shared in-flight entry carry both the task and its diagnostics, or otherwise delay visibility until the winning `NewLoad` attribution is established.

proposed_comments.title: Stop accepting new diagnostics once a session starts stopping

confidence.rationale: These entry points continue accepting new requests, loads, and UI-probe updates while Stop is gathering the final session snapshot, which leaves the report window mutable.

proposed_comments.title: Flip the stopped flag before capturing stop-time snapshots

confidence.rationale: Stop captures the end timestamp and then performs several final measurements before publishing the stopped flag, leaving a window where late callbacks can still mutate counters.

proposed_comments.body:
### Flip the stopped flag before capturing stop-time snapshots

**Severity:** `medium`

Inside `IconLoadDiagnosticsSession.Stop()`, the stopped timestamp is currently published only after the process, GC, and working-set snapshots are collected. That leaves a window where late request or load callbacks still see the session as active and mutate counters after `EndedUtc` has effectively been chosen. Please publish the stop cutoff before those final measurements are gathered.

proposed_comments.title: Ignore late request updates after stop

confidence.rationale: RequestMeasurement retains the session reference and its resolution, invalidation, and completion methods all continue mutating session state unless they check the stopped flag.

proposed_comments.title: Ignore late load updates after stop

confidence.rationale: LoadMeasurement retains the session reference and still updates enqueue, worker, dispatcher, and completion counters after Stop unless each mutation path is guarded.

proposed_comments.title: Classify Windows shell-binary paths case-insensitively

confidence.rationale: Windows executable, DLL, and shortcut paths are case-insensitive, but the current classification uses case-sensitive suffix checks and misreports uppercase shell-binary inputs.

proposed_comments.body:
### Classify Windows shell-binary paths case-insensitively

**Severity:** `medium`

Windows paths are case-insensitive, so values like `APP.EXE`, `tool.DLL`, and `shortcut.LNK` should still be counted as shell binaries. The current ordinal check reports them as generic strings and skews the diagnostics; please update the matching test expectation as well.

```suggestion
            if (path.EndsWith(".exe", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
                || path.EndsWith(".dll", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
                || path.EndsWith(".lnk", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
```
